cover.note: degree-3 map, defined over Q(sqrt(-1)), from y^2 = g to a genus-1 curve; found by code/gsplit_cover3.m (torsion_jac, 2026-10-16)

notes: First Q-simple, geometrically split example of [9] for the census (the gsplit cell is empty). Found by querying the LMFDB genus 2 data (devmirror.lmfdb.xyz, g2c_curves: is_simple_base = true, is_simple_geom = false); smallest-conductor curve of this torsion group there (LMFDB conductor 1696). The automatic Richelot certificates do not apply (over Q(sqrt(-1)) the working model factors as two cubics and has no Richelot isogeny), so a splitness certificate is supplied: an explicit degree-3 map to a genus-1 curve over Q(sqrt(-1)) (the field over which J splits; the cubic factors of g are the fibre over the point at infinity and the three remaining Weierstrass points). Checked locally with the census's own pipeline/magma/verify_lib.m (Magma V2.30-1). Submitted by F. Najman; the curve is due to the database cited under Reference, the cover was computed for this submission.
